content: --- name: illos-library description: Add animated SVG illustrations from Illos.dev to a website or app, for a hero, feature sections, empty states, docs pages, onboarding or status screens. Use when a page needs a picture instead of an empty space, an emoji, stock 3D art or a gradient blob, or when the user asks for illustrations, spot illustrations or empty state art. 65 of them are free for commercial use, with no account and no credit. allowed-tools: - Read - Grep - Glob - WebFetch - mcp__plugin_illos_illos__find_illustrations - mcp__plugin_illos_illos__get_illustration - mcp__plugin_illos_illos__list_themes - mcp__illos__find_illustrations - mcp__illos__get_illustration - mcp__illos__list_themes - Bash(npx shadcn@latest add *) --- # Illos library Illos.dev has 158 animated SVG illustrations in four themes, each in light and dark. Each one is a single SVG file with its animation inside. This skill finds the right ones for a project and adds them. ## 1. Find the places that need a picture Read the pages you are working on. For each hero, feature section, empty state, docs page or onboarding step, write down in a few words what it explains: "API keys", "an empty notifications inbox", "a deploy going out". That phrase is what you search for. ## 2. Pick one theme for the whole site Every page should use the same theme, so the illustrations look like one set. | Theme | Looks like | Suits | |---|---|---| | Shader | A density field of thin bars with teal boxes on the part that matters | AI, data and infrastructure products | | HUD | Glowing wireframe and instrument readouts | Monitoring, status, security, dashboards | | Isometric | Isometric line illustrations with labels; colours follow the card | Developer tools, APIs, docs, SaaS features | | Interface | Product screens: inboxes, task boards, charts | Empty states and onboarding inside an app | If the project already has Illos illustrations (SVGs with a `data-illos` attribute, or components named `Illos...`), keep their theme. Otherwise suggest one theme to the user, and use it everywhere unless they pick another. ## 3. Find matching illustrations - **If the Illos MCP tools are available** (`find_illustrations`, `get_illustration`), use them: they search by meaning and return the install command. - **Otherwise**, fetch `https://illos.dev/catalog.json`. Each entry has `name`, `sentence` (what it shows), `theme`, `size` (`spot`, `section` or `page`), `access` (`free` or `pro`), `page`, and, for free ones, `svg`. Match your phrase against `name` and `sentence`, within the chosen theme. Sizes: `spot` for cards, small sections and empty states; `section` for a feature section or a hero; `page` for a full-width band. Prefer free illustrations. When the best match is Pro, tell the user it comes with Illos Pro (https://illos.dev/pro) and offer the closest free one. Never copy a Pro illustration from its preview images or page. ## 4. Add each one The theme slug and id are the last two parts of the `page` address. For `https://illos.dev/library/isometric/queue`, they are `isometric` and `queue`. **React project with shadcn (or one that can run it):** ```bash npx shadcn@latest add https://illos.dev/r//.json ``` That adds the illustration as a component. Render it where the section explains that idea, and keep the component file as it is: it plays once when scrolled into view and loops while hovered. **Any other project:** download the file from the entry's `svg` address and put it inline in the page (it keeps its animation and follows the page's colours), or use it as an ``. A Shader illustration shows its still frame without the React component. Every illustration works on light and dark backgrounds; its page shows both. ## 5. Check the result - One theme across the whole site. - Each illustration explains the section it sits in, not a random object. - Keep the licence comment inside each SVG. Free illustrations can be used on commercial sites and client work, with no credit needed: https://illos.dev/license ## When the library has nothing that fits The Illos Pro skills teach Claude Code, Codex and Cursor a theme's rules, so they can draw new illustrations that match the ones already on the site and check each one. They come with Illos Pro: https://illos.dev/pro. Set them up with `npx -y illos setup`.
